summary: Polygon's Susana Polo interviews Dropout CEO Sam Reich and Dimension 20 host Brennan Lee Mulligan on Dropout's fifth anniversary. Reich announced in an anniversary video that the company will stop using the CollegeHumor name, something the team had wanted since Dropout formed. They also discuss the upcoming Dimension 20 season Burrow's End, building a sustainable business beyond algorithm-driven platforms, improv, and new show announcements like Very Important People.
one_line: On Dropout's fifth anniversary, Sam Reich and Brennan Lee Mulligan explain dropping the CollegeHumor name, their business model, improv work and upcoming shows.
key_facts: Dropout launched as a subscription service in late 2018, and IAC stopped funding CH Media, leading to layoffs of nearly the entire staff in January 2020.
IAC sold the CollegeHumor brand to executive producer Sam Reich, allowing Dimension 20, Um, Actually, and Game Changer to continue.
Brennan Lee Mulligan says CollegeHumor is "the most healthy and sustainable [it's] ever been as a company."
For the fifth anniversary, Sam Reich announced in a video that the company will cease to be CollegeHumor.
The next Dimension 20 season is Burrow's End, run by Aabria Iyengar, a Secret of NIMH/Watership Down-style story about stoats and other critters.
Mulligan says Dimension 20 has most success when it gets specific, e.g. Game of Thrones meets Candyland.
Reich's advice to creators is to find a better business model, offering something off the algorithm-driven platforms, such as a Patreon-style subscription or Hollywood opportunities.
The name was "Dropout" rather than "CollegeHumor Plus" or "Pro" because the team wanted to distance themselves from the CollegeHumor brand and its frat-y roots.
Reich says Dropout shifted to more unscripted content after breaking from IAC, because scripted content didn't work well on the platform.
Wayne Brady, a guest on Make Some Noise, reportedly said "There are only two people doing taped improv correctly: us and you."
Very Important People is a reboot of the CollegeHumor show Hello My Name Is, in which Josh Ruben did interviews in makeup; Vic Michaelis hosts the new version.
Reich says Adam Conover compared digital creation to a jail you must live in forever; Reich and Mulligan say they jailed themselves in anthology series.
Mulligan says he really ate an entire bag of Cool Ranch Doritos, hidden in a Chompsky's bag, in the announcement video.
